key_insight: Higher-order binary optimization (HUBO) can reduce qubit count for logistics and scheduling problems, but the gain comes at the cost of deeper circuits and harder hardware execution.
engineering_relevance: For industrial routing and scheduling, HUBO may better preserve real workflow constraints than QUBO, making it relevant for near-term hybrid optimization and future fault-tolerant quantum systems.
method: Formulated three logistics/manufacturing cases as HUBO problems.
Compared HUBO encodings against corresponding QUBO formulations.
Validated the models with classical solvers and simulated bias-field digitized counterdiabatic quantum optimization on small routing instances.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports classical validation across several instances plus resource and scalability analysis for capacitated vehicle routing to assess qubit demand and implementation feasibility.
watch_item: Higher-order interactions increase circuit depth, so current noisy hardware may negate the qubit-saving advantage unless fidelity and coherence improve.
paper_title: Quantum optimization beyond QUBO for industrial logistics and scheduling
